elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Subparagraph 18.1A: "Teleglobe USA Inc. (the "Customer") may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, including during the Initial Period". "Terminate its participation" is the exit mechanic this consortium agreement itself uses in 18.1, so the right is operative notwithstanding that the deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" keyed on the model phrase "terminate this Agreement ... for convenience" and returned false; in substance the Customer-side convenience right is expressly rendered.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice thereof to the other Parties" — 30 days, in writing, and no additional consent, cure, or Management Committee condition is layered on the Customer's election (the "Notwithstanding Subparagraph 18.1" opener disapplies the one-year/end-of-term constraint).

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "the other Parties shall refund to the Customer, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by it in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination" — the words "pro rata" are express (not inferred from the post-termination period alone), the payer is the counterparty side, and "any amounts prepaid" necessarily captures prepaid fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already satisfied by retained text and correctly left un-redrafted: 18.1 permits a Party to withdraw only "at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter" on one year's notice — natural-term exit assessed under RENEWAL, not mid-term T4C — and 18.2 permits mid-term termination only "by agreement in writing of all the Parties" or a 90% Management Committee majority, i.e. no unilateral counterparty convenience right during the 25-year Initial Period. 18.1A is drafted for the named Customer alone and creates no reciprocal counterparty right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 18.1A sets 30 days, which is better than the fallback band but does not literally satisfy "60 to 90 days". Immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee is imposed on a withdrawal under 18.1A, so no cap is needed. The retained forfeiture sentence is expressly confined to "a Party that terminates its participation in accordance with Subparagraph 18.1" and does not reach the new, separately numbered 18.1A right.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: 18.1 confines any Party's unilateral withdrawal to "the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter"; mid-term exit under 18.2 requires unanimity or a 90% majority.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.1 requires "not less than one (1) year's prior notice ... in writing, to the other Parties", exceeding the 90-day floor.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted Subparagraph 18.1A carries the three missing elements (Customer-only convenience right, 30 days' written notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts), and the fourth element was already met by retained 18.1/18.2, which the drafter correctly did not re-draft.

The failing deterministic check ("Customer convenience termination present") is a phrasing-pattern miss, not a substantive gap: 18.1A states the Customer "may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, including during the Initial Period", mirroring the agreement's own 18.1 exit vocabulary. No repair required.

Minimal: one concise insertion into a document that had no Customer convenience exit; nothing was deleted or paraphrased, favourable retained language (one-year counterparty notice, unanimity/90% mid-term gate) survives, and no extras were added — no survival tail, no at-own-expense wording, no notice/procedure boilerplate, no damages categories, and no duplicate operative refund or fee mechanic.

Preserves intent: 18.1, 18.2, the paragraph 3 Management Committee cross-reference and the capital-cost sentence all remain intact and internally consistent. Because the forfeiture sentence is drafted by express reference to "Subparagraph 18.1" only, it does not contradict or penalise a withdrawal under the new 18.1A, and no term is left undefined or dangling (the "Customer" label is defined in-line in 18.1A).

Residual drafting note (rationale-level only, not an element failure): the capital-cost no-credit sentence is silent as to 18.1A. The current numbering means it cannot attach, but if the counterparty argues otherwise the cleanest cure is to append "in accordance with Subparagraph 18.1 (and not Subparagraph 18.1A)" rather than to expand 18.1A; that money term is properly held for the liquidated-damages rule to avoid double-flagging.
Fallback level is not independently complete (30 days sits outside the 60–90 day band), which is immaterial since the preferred checklist is fully met and the comment offers the fallback as a trade.
